title: Edge On‑Prem Evening Sync: tactical observations and triage
content:
Evening sync notes from the install team — quick capture before we fragment. Mostly raw, triage-first.

Context and goal:
- Customer: enterprise-fintech (US-east). VPC + onprem redis cache in DMZ.
- Primary ask: deterministic latency under 60ms P95 for small (128 token) completions.
- Tonight's focus: finish node pool rollout, unblock model load failures, surface remaining network edges.

SYNOPSIS (short):
- Major blocker: two onprem nodes repeatedly failing model load (hang at model::init -> nvml driver mismatch). Suspect driver/quantization lib mismatch.
- Secondary blocker: intermittent TLS handshake failures between field-proxy and control plane (GRPC ECONNRESET when TLS renegotiation occurrs). Likely corporate proxy doing TLS interception on HTTP/2.
- Networking: MTU mismatch observed on site-facing trunk -> causes ~1% packet drops at >=9000B payloads. Symptoms show up in long tail token latency.

TIMELINE / RUNS:
- 2026-06-19 14:00 local: preflight passed on paper (SSH, KMS vesting, disk), but nobody ran nvidia-smi after driver install.
- 2026-06-19 16:30: first model load attempt -> 2 nodes hung at model::kv_cache_init. Logs show nvml reports driver 525.85 but CUDA toolkit runtime expects 530.x.
- 2026-06-19 18:00: rolled back to CPU build for the hung nodes (temporary). Throughput dropped 34% but customer test path green.
- 2026-06-20 09:15: observed 5 TLS handshake failures per hour in proxy logs; correlated with corporate proxy appliance (BlueCoil) doing TLS rewrap.
- 2026-06-21 11:40: spike of packet drops when bulk model warmup occurred (MTU fragmentation).

OBSERVATIONS / EVIDENCE:
- Node logs (node-03, node-07): repeated lines: "ERROR model_loader.cpp:211 - failed to open /usr/lib/libcublas.so.11: version `CUBLAS_11.4' not found" (matches mismatch hypothesis).
- dmesg snippet (node-07): occasional NIC driver dropped packet counters incrementing when STRESS warmup runs.
- Field-proxy logs: "grpc: encountered connection error: EOF" and TLS handshake alerts: "received unexpected message (40)".
- tcpdump snippet: SYN, SYN/ACK fine; handshake dies during TLS ClientHello extensions (HTTP/2 specific ALPN failing). Corporate proxy inserts a custom cert (subject CN=BlueCoil Proxy).

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS (assigned):
- Aisha: push a short helper script to preflight that checks CUDA runtime vs installed driver (ENG-4321). Must run before lib installs. Due: 2026-06-23 EOD.
- Liam: onboard field-net to run MTU probe across all site trunk ports and adjust jumbo config; document safe MTU for hosted <-> site paths. Due: 2026-06-24 AM.
- Marisol: engage customer infra/security to confirm BlueCoil proxy cert pinning workarounds. Short-term: we will negotiate bypass for control-plane endpoints and set GRPC to use TLS with explicit SNI mapping. Blocker: customer change window required. Due: 2026-06-25.
- Omar: test a rebuild of the 525->530 driver path in lab, attempt to reproduce cublas missing symbol error; if reproducible, craft a remediation script that updates symlinks and validates lib versions. Due: 2026-06-24.

RISK NOTES / MITIGATIONS:
- Risk: If customer cannot relax proxy interception, we will have to route control-plane traffic via a dedicated egress (longer lead). Mitigation: enable mutual TLS with pinned CAs (adds config complexity).
- Risk: Driver mismatch during install is high-probability across older colo sites. Mitigation: add driver/runtime matrix to field checklist + automated detection.
- Risk: MTU fragmentation impacts P95/99 cost numbers and causes retried requests that burn token budget. Mitigation: force smaller GSO/TSO settings in kernel as stopgap and plan for trunk MTU alignment.

DEEPER NOTES (less formal):
- Notes to self: make preflight "nvidia sanity" show a friendly warning and a one-liner to apt/yum install targeted driver. Right now the install playbook assumes driver is correct. Bad assumption.
- Possible host-level quickfix: LD_PRELOAD shim to provide missing symbol for older libcublas builds? Risky and ugly — avoid unless we must.
- Observed pattern: whenever heavy KV cache warmup runs concurrently with model loads, NIC drops rise. Hypothesis: irqbalance not tuned or SR-IOV vf default queuing wrong. Put this on SRE deep-dive.

OPEN QUESTIONS / DECISIONS NEEDED:
- Do we require a change window to request customer to modify BlueCoil proxy rules, or can we tunnel control-plane over a preapproved port? (owner: Marisol)
- Should preflight auto-block the install if driver/runtime mismatch found, or only warn? (owner: Eng Leads)
- We currently fallback to CPU build automatically on model load fail — that preserves correctness but can hide infra flakiness. Should fallback be opt-in per-customer? (owner: Product-hosted-api)

FOLLOWUPS / NEXT CHECKPOINTS:
- 2026-06-23 09:00 sync: validate preflight script + run a lab reproduction of cublas error.
- 2026-06-24 11:00 field-net MTU report + proposed kernel GSO workaround.
- 2026-06-25 16:00 customer security decision on proxy.

QUICK WIN IDEAS (for retention):
- Add a small binary to the installer that performs live nvml/cuda checks and recommends exact driver package strings per distro. Less friction for field.
- Expose a lightweight health endpoint that the field-proxy can call which returns the full list of loaded libs + versions (for faster triage). Ensure no secrets in response.

RETRO - things to capture into playbook once stable:
- explicit step: run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` and fail fast if runtime mismatch detected; include recommended apt/yum strings.
- document that corporate TLS interception is a common blocker — add decision tree: pin CA, request bypass, or route via backhaul.

MISC NOTES / fragments:
- "customer wants 60ms P95 but scoping warms up 10x tokens in test -> unrealistic test; ask for a realistic SLO test harness"
- TODO: capture exact tcpdump pcap and attach to ENG-4321 thread.

END OF NOTES.

-- Aisha (field lead)
